Action Plan:
1. Prescribe Fexofenadine 180 mg orally once daily for symptomatic relief of pruritus; advise patient to start today.
2. Prescribe Betnovate (betamethasone valerate 0.1%) ointment; apply a thin “fingertip unit” twice daily to affected areas (chest, arms, hands, antecubital fossae) for 14 days, then reassess.
3. Continue regular emollient therapy: Diprobase cream liberally and Dermol soap substitute for bathing.
4. Educate on gentle skin care: avoid hot showers, fragrance-free detergents, keep nails short to reduce excoriation risk.
5. Follow-up: if no improvement or worsening at any time, book review sooner; otherwise routine review in 2 weeks.
6. Prescriptions to be sent to patient’s nominated Boots pharmacy for same-day collection.
7. Asthma stable; continue salbutamol (blue inhaler) PRN and seek care if respiratory symptoms flare.
8. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
• Reason for visit: 3-day history of worsening eczema with widespread sore, red, dry, very itchy patches on chest, hands, arms, especially antecubital fossae. No weeping, no thickened skin. Cracking present but no infection signs.  
• No fever, joint pain, or systemic symptoms.  
Past Medical History  
• Atopic eczema (chronic)  
• Asthma (intermittent)  
Family History  
• Mother: hypothyroidism, migraine  
Medications  
• Diprobase cream (dose/frequency not documented)  
• Dermol wash (dose/frequency not documented)  
• OTC hydrocortisone 1% cream (ineffective)  
• Salbutamol inhaler PRN (dose/frequency not documented)  
Allergies  
• No known drug allergies  
Social History  
• Not recorded

Objective:
No in-person examination performed (telehealth). Patient reports:  
• Skin: widespread erythematous, dry, cracked, intensely pruritic patches on chest, bilateral arms, hands, antecubital fossae. No exudate, no lichenification, no excoriations reported.  
• General: afebrile, systemically well by history.  
(No vitals obtained; no other system exams performed.)

Assessment & Plan:

1. Extensive eczema flare
   - Assessment: Acute exacerbation of chronic atopic dermatitis.
   - Investigations: None at this stage; clinical diagnosis.
   - Treatment: Betnovate ointment BID ×14 days; continue emollients; skin care education.
   - Follow-up: Review in 2 weeks or sooner if deterioration.

2. Pruritus secondary to eczema
   - Assessment: Atopic pruritus.
   - Treatment: Fexofenadine 180 mg daily.
   - Follow-up: As above.

3. Asthma (stable)
   - Assessment: Intermittent, mild; currently asymptomatic.
   - Treatment: Continue salbutamol inhaler PRN.
   - Follow-up: Routine; reinforce need for review if increased use.

Quality checks:

• Missing expected elements: vitals, smoking/alcohol history, full medication doses/frequencies, immunization status.  
• Internal conflicts: Doctor restated “hyperthyroidism” but patient said mother has hypothyroidism—conflict noted.  
• Transcript quality: Clear; minor overlaps but clinically adequate.
